The election daemon and config-wallet pool command obtain the complete authorization from engine.validator.createPqStakeAuthorization and route to an admitted controller through a pool; the daemon's no-pool branch and the interactive wallet-to-elector command refuse locally before building or sending a stake. The base validator-elect Fift tools may be removed only in the same change that migrates every retained caller, updates test-smartcont.cpp, and leaves neither pool tooling nor tests with dangling references.
classical-stake-producers-incompatible-w.observation: The PQ elector rejects the classical 0x654C5074 stake authorization. The two base validator-election Fift tools, Validator.fif's validator-elect-req>B word, the C++ smart-contract test, two Fift proposal tests, nominator-pool-lifecycle-e2e.py, and both pool operator scripts still produce or consume it; validator-election-stage-a.py was a caller at discovery but has since been cleared. The three previously found tosctl stake paths no longer locally sign this preimage: the election daemon and config-wallet pool command obtain node authorization and route through the production pool builder, while the interactive direct-to-elector bid refuses locally. Within validator-election-stage-a.py, the no-argument launch-gate passed a complete three-election PQ rehearsal at exact source commit 60a299125. The explicit experiment mode was then converted separately at 471e0a027: it has no classical Fift/local-sign path, uses node authorization and the production pool body, attributes elector credit to pool stake owners, and matches live ConfigParam 34 by controller/ADNL. Its exact-tree 600+600-second diagnostic report has SHA-256 d04b4a111d004e5466838f25f85e568bf0dd2c84c5649de5f39402188b2199df; both elections activated four controller IDs, eight pool stakes were accepted, and four matured first-round pool credits recovered. Four successor stakes remained active-retained and unrecovered at this run's end; their recovery behavior was not exercised by this live run. A separate 600+900-second exact-tree run at 8dd38d088 (report SHA-256 2a29b4f79be100410497be277890af6bcd6af163714d1f8a0b6a59dc3495e1ad) reached an estimated unfreeze timestamp while the successor was still live ConfigParam 34. The v4 instrument wrongly marked those four active stakes matured and failed with four outstanding; Elector check_unfreeze requires a non-active set and update_active_vset_id resets the actual unfreeze time on retirement. This is an instrument classification defect, not a failed pool recovery. The corrected instrument uses current ConfigParam 34 cell hash plus Elector past_elections_list actual unfreeze time; the default three-election Stage A, not experiment mode, supplies the live second-round recovery evidence. This script is cleared as a live classical Fift caller, while the remaining retained Fift callers keep this question OPEN. single-nominator-pool's contract is already converted, but its operator script is stale. liquid-staking's controller still sends classical new_stake directly to the elector and handles new_stake_ok/new_stake_error, so liquid-staking is not launch-supported. Pooled staking remains in the launch set through the converted single-nominator path; liquid-staking must not appear in a release claim until its contract-level conversion is complete. A separate PQ identity regression in the tosctl daemon compared the elector's validator_id with an Ed25519 ADNL transport public key, and the finished-election check compared that validator_id with the operator wallet. e2d0b3e7d changed both to controller identity and added distinct-id behavioral fixtures; this fixes participant recognition but does not close the remaining classical-stake tooling question.
classical-stake-producers-incompatible-w.t3_current_state: The multi-nominator lifecycle script's classical Fift caller has been removed in the T3 static conversion: it provisions four Genesis controller-bound PQ validators plus one noninitial controller-bound spare, reads back the genesis-installed ConfigParam 47 policy, obtains node stake authorization, passes a controller birth witness through the production pool builder, and checks live ConfigParam 34 by controller/ADNL pairing. Eight exact executable files still retain the inventoried Fift tool/word dependency. The single-nominator operator Fift script and the two launch-facing tosctl witness handoffs remain OPEN; liquid staking remains outside launch support.

merkle-base-state-mismatch.observation: Two recovered error lines from test-consensus-simplex2-pq-finality-e2e-100 under whole-suite parallel load show the same one-height mismatch. At 68ea21db4 on 2026-09-22 07:02:35 UTC, StateResolver actors 87 and 77 reported the same invalid Merkle update 4 ms apart: the update expected synthetic fixture state seqno 5 but the resolver applied it to seqno 4. At efd22ce46 on 2026-09-22 12:46:23 UTC, StateResolver actor 83 reported expected seqno 23, applied to seqno 22. The four hashes were independently decoded against the fixture state encoding; original BOCs, candidate IDs and stacks were not retained. Source: memo/pq-native/N6-MERKLE-RECOVERED-EVIDENCE-20260923.md. This establishes a missing one-block state transition on the resolver's path, not which component omitted it; H2 (skipping a block-referencing empty candidate), a skip/anchor shortcut, and a stale fixture-manager state remain hypotheses, not diagnoses.

pool-first-stake-birth-witness-missing.observation: At discovery, both launch-facing pool callers obtained node-bound PQ authorization but called nominator::new_stake, which fixed the optional controller birth witness to None; the Elector returns reason 8 for such a first stake. They now share an optional NodeBinding locator for the original deployment StateInit BOC and a builder that compares node authorization, pool controller identity and live ConfigParam 47 dictionary membership before emitting a witnessed pool order. Missing and mismatched inputs refuse locally in tests. Old configurations remain readable but cannot first-stake without this public artifact. The new config bind import-birth command extracts the public StateInit from an operator-supplied deployment transaction BOC, verifies its transaction account, message destination and derived identity against the configured controller, and binds a create-new artifact to an idle node. This is offline shape/identity verification, not independent chain-finality proof. Existing deployment commands still do not create the controller or own its birth artifact. Neither product caller has a real first STAKE_ACCEPTED or live ConfigParam 34 result. Stage A's passing fixture and the static multi-nominator lifecycle route cannot supply that product evidence. See T3-POOL-OPERATOR-AUDIT.md. Liquid staking remains outside the launch set.
pool-first-stake-birth-witness-missing.t3_handoff_plan: Retain the controller deployment transaction BOC and import its original StateInit through config bind import-birth; current mutable account data is not a birth artifact. Both product callers read the bound artifact, compare it with node and pool identity, require code membership in live ConfigParam 47 and build through the shared verified witness path before wallet send.
